subject.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): add timeouts to model discovery requests

question: Should Amazon Bedrock discovery enforce an unconditional 30-second deadline for every foundation-model and inference-profile page request?
rationale: The patch is technically sound, but choosing a fixed deadline intentionally trades indefinite setup/catalog hangs for empty or partial discovery on unusually slow valid control-plane responses; tests cannot determine that product availability policy.

options.title: Accept the 30-second deadline
options.body: Keep the focused provider-local constant and existing graceful fallbacks, then refresh and validate the exact head before merge.

options.title: Choose a different bounded policy
options.body: Request a different constant or a broader shared discovery-timeout design, avoiding a new user config option unless a concrete need clears the repository's config-surface bar.

options.title: Retain provider-controlled waiting
options.body: Close or pause the PR and continue allowing Bedrock discovery calls to wait without an OpenClaw deadline.

recommendation.title: Accept the 30-second deadline
recommendation.body: Keep the focused provider-local constant and existing graceful fallbacks, then refresh and validate the exact head before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the current inference-profile discovery behavior and are best positioned among the traced history owners to accept its new availability boundary.
